summary: Our project inspires young minds to explore the wonders of the universe while demonstrating that gathering intelligence and strategic data is often more valuable than simply winning. Through hands-on learning, participants discover the fundamental engineering, scientific, and logistical components required to operate a theoretical Martian base. By simulating real-world space exploration challenges, we foster critical thinking, curiosity, and problem-solving skills. Ultimately, our mission is to equip the next generation with a deeper understanding of aerospace fundamentals, showing them that true success in space—and in life—depends on thorough preparation, continuous learning, and the pursuit of knowledge.
details:
• Goal: Survive 5 sols (Martian days) on the base by repairing damaged modules and managing resources.
  • View: Top-down (similar to Red Dust Colony). Clicking a module opens a panel displaying data and an educational description.
  • Target Audience: Children aged 7–12 (matching the theme), while remaining engaging for older siblings and parents through an advanced mode with detailed numbers. Every decision has a visible consequence, without requiring complicated math.
  • Location: Elysium Planitia on Mars, the landing site of the InSight probe, which allows the game's database to use real weather data from the InSight mission.
  • Platform: Web browser (Unity WebGL), with no downloads or accounts required.
  • Time: 1 sol lasts approximately 60 seconds, with the timer ending the day automatically. A full playthrough takes about 5–6 minutes, with the remainder of the demo serving as a walkthrough.
  • Core Gameplay Loop: Each sol, the player gets 3 Action Points (AP) to spend on repairs, rover expeditions, taking shelter, and starting up the reactor. Players can also toggle ECO mode on modules for 0 AP.
  • Winning: Survive all 5 sols. The final score depends on the condition of the base and the number of research points earned (see Section 12).
    • Scenario: A fixed sequence designed for the demo.
    • Random Mission: Features different failures and events in every playthrough.
    • NASA Data: Generates events using a random window of real archival data (see Section 8.2).
  • Losing: Oxygen drops to 0 at the end of a sol, Radiation reaches 100, or Base Health (HP) drops to 0 or below.
    1. Everything consumes energy.
    2. Ignoring a failure causes it to worsen.
    3. Saving power (ECO mode) reduces production.
    4. Conducting research and going outside costs oxygen, energy, and increases radiation exposure.
